findings.title: Point-event clip export always rejects
findings.why_it_matters: Users cannot export clips for hits or bounces from the desktop event UI: the shared event contract requires point events to have end equal to start, while this handler forwards that zero-length interval to an exporter that requires start to be strictly less than end. Every normal hit/bounce reaches the same deterministic error. Expanding point events to a bounded interval around the timestamp, as the iOS ClipExporter already does, makes the advertised event export usable while preserving rally intervals.
findings.suggested_fix: In make_clip, load the video duration and convert start == end into a bounded window such as max(0, start - 2) through min(duration, end + 2), matching ios/TennisApp/AnalysisEngine.swift; keep explicit start/end for rallies.
evidence: src/tennis_ai/library.py:58 -- or not 0 <= start < end <= summary["video"]["duration"]
src/tennis_ai/events.py:35-36 -- if event["kind"] != "rally" and event["end"] != event["start"]: raise ValueError("Point events must have identical start/end times")

findings.title: Incomplete imports are silently marked complete
findings.why_it_matters: An analysis folder missing frames, events, or corrections is accepted, and the new store is then marked complete. A damaged transfer can therefore appear successfully imported while silently losing predictions or durable human edits; the Start/Continue action also returns immediately because the store says complete. Requiring the declared artifacts and preserving the manifest status prevents corrupt or paused packages from being converted into false completions.
findings.suggested_fix: Reject a package when any required artifact declared by manifest.artifacts is missing, import each required file, and initialize the store status from manifest.status instead of unconditionally setting .complete; only a manifest that is complete should produce a complete imported store.
evidence: ios/TennisApp/Library.swift:73-74 -- if FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath:input.path) { try FileManager.default.copyItem(at:input,to:target) } else if relative==manifest.media.path { throw PackageError.invalid("Source video is missing from package") }

findings.title: Swift accepts positions on non-bounce events
findings.why_it_matters: A portable package containing a hit or rally with a position passes the Swift importer and can be re-exported, but the desktop contract validator rejects the same record because court positions are bounce-only. That breaks round-trip interoperability for an input the native side claims is valid. Enforcing the shared semantic rule in AnalysisEvent.validate keeps both implementations aligned.
findings.suggested_fix: In AnalysisEvent.validate, reject non-nil position unless kind == .bounce, then add a shared-fixture/import test for a hit carrying position and assert that both Swift and Python reject it.
evidence: ios/Sources/TennisCore/Contract.swift:121 -- if let p = position { guard p.count == 2, p.allSatisfy(\.isFinite) else { throw PackageError.invalid("Invalid court position") } }
ios/TennisApp/Library.swift:87 -- for event in events.events { try store.saveEvent(event,duration:manifest.media.duration) }
src/tennis_ai/events.py:59-60 -- if event["kind"] != "bounce" or not isinstance(point, (list, tuple)) or len(point) != 2: raise ValueError("Only bounce events can have a court position [x, y]")

residual_risks: The simulator smoke test exercises a short valid complete-package round trip, but it does not establish physical-device behavior, long-run thermal/storage recovery, or imported paused-package semantics.

Package manifests authenticate the source video but do not checksum frames, events, or corrections, so post-export corruption of analysis artifacts is detected only when parsing or structural invariants happen to fail.
testing_gaps: No desktop UI/integration test exports a hit or bounce whose contract-valid end equals start.
No iOS import test covers a missing required artifact or a paused/inference-complete manifest.
Shared contract tests do not include semantically invalid cross-platform events such as a hit with a court position.
